questions.stem: According to collision theory, what conditions are needed for a successful collision?

options.text: Particles must collide with any amount of energy
Particles must collide with sufficient energy and in the correct orientation
Particles must be at the same temperature and pressure
Particles must be in the same physical state

questions.explanation: Collision theory states that for a reaction to occur, particles must collide with energy equal to or greater than the activation energy AND in the correct orientation. If either condition is not met, the particles simply bounce apart without reacting.

questions.stem: Using collision theory, what is the main reason that increasing temperature has such a large effect on reaction rate?

options.text: Particles collide more frequently because they move faster
A much greater proportion of collisions have energy equal to or greater than the activation energy
The activation energy is reduced at higher temperatures
More particles are created at higher temperatures

questions.explanation: While particles do move faster at higher temperatures (causing more frequent collisions), the main reason for the large effect is that a much greater proportion of collisions are energetic enough to overcome the activation energy barrier. This means many more collisions result in successful reactions.
